articles.title: We re-ran our MCP scanner comparison on 14,933 npm and PyPI tool lists, in gVisor, with two more scanners
articles.excerpt: A week ago we ran three MCP security scanners on a tool-poisoning benchmark and 986 real servers. Three things in that post were weak. The real servers were all remote HTTP servers, while most local M…
articles.body: A week ago we ran three MCP security scanners on a tool-poisoning benchmark and 986 real servers . Three things in that post were weak. The real servers were all remote HTTP servers, while most local MCP tools are npm and PyPI packages. We compared only two other scanners. And it all ran on a workstation. So we ran it again: five scanners instead of three, 14,933 package tool lists next to the 986 servers, and every scanner, ours included, in a gVisor container with no network. Here is what moved, and what didn't. What didn't move Our scanner, WARDEN, went from ruleset v10 to v12 in the week between. v11 decodes escapes, HTML entities, percent encoding and base64 before the rules run; v12 stops excusing a quoted attack phrase when the sentence asks the model to carry it out.

articles.title: Migrating books between providers: tying opening balances to bank statements, with uncleared items
articles.excerpt: When books move between providers, the new ledger opens with the old provider's last balance sheet. Each bank and card balance on it must equal the bank's printed statement for that day, plus or minus…
articles.body: When books move between providers, the new ledger opens with the old provider's last balance sheet. Each bank and card balance on it must equal the bank's printed statement for that day, plus or minus uncleared items such as an uncashed check. The rule is difference = 0 . An unexplained gap means the old books need another look first. That is a data validation problem with a very clear rule, so it is worth writing as code. I work on ZeraBooks, where we set opening balances this way for businesses moving from Bench and elsewhere. All figures below are fictional. What data do you need for an opening balance tie-out? Two sources per account: the closing balance sheet from the old provider, and the printed statement balance from the bank, both on the cutover date.

articles.title: InboxWall: How a Local-First MCP Server Sanitizes Email HTML to Stop Prompt Injection Before the LLM Sees It
articles.excerpt: Email is a hostile data source. When you give an AI agent access to your inbox, you hand it HTML that may contain hidden CSS directives, Unicode obfuscation, and invisible text designed to manipulate…
articles.body: Email is a hostile data source. When you give an AI agent access to your inbox, you hand it HTML that may contain hidden CSS directives, Unicode obfuscation, and invisible text designed to manipulate the LLM's context window. InboxWall is an open-source MCP server that sanitizes email HTML before the agent sees it, running entirely on your local machine. The project exposes a key architectural question: where should security boundaries live in agent tool chains? InboxWall's answer is to treat sanitization as a preprocessing step that happens outside the LLM's trust boundary, implemented as a standalone MCP server that other agents can call. Why Email HTML Is a Prompt Injection Vector Email clients render HTML, CSS, and Unicode to display formatted messages.

articles.title: Time-Blocking Automation: What Akiflow Exposes About Agent Scheduling Primitives
articles.excerpt: Akiflow's unified calendar-task view solves a human problem: merging scattered to-dos with calendar availability so you can drag tasks into realistic time slots. The plumbing underneath that drag-and-…
articles.body: Akiflow's unified calendar-task view solves a human problem: merging scattered to-dos with calendar availability so you can drag tasks into realistic time slots. The plumbing underneath that drag-and-drop interface is the same infrastructure agents need when they schedule their own execution windows, book API calls around rate limits, or coordinate multi-step workflows across time. The 105-point Hacker News discussion around Akiflow's YC launch exposed sustained developer interest in time-planning tools. What matters for agent builders is not the UI, but the primitives: How do you represent task duration estimates programmatically? How do you resolve scheduling conflicts when an agent queries three external calendars? What's the API contract for "find me two hours before Friday"?

articles.title: Your Secure Element Was Never The Target
articles.excerpt: The Ledger implant heist didn't break crypto. It bypassed it entirely by watching the screen. Everyone told you to buy a hardware wallet. Cold storage. Secure Element. Never expose your seed. And it w…
articles.body: The Ledger implant heist didn't break crypto. It bypassed it entirely by watching the screen. Everyone told you to buy a hardware wallet. Cold storage. Secure Element. Never expose your seed. And it was good advice, right up until someone realized you don't need to hack the vault if you can just read the sticky note as the owner writes it down. This week the story finally broke wide. On Oct 13, Kim Zetter at Zero Day published what researchers had been whispering about for months: implants found in Ledger and Trezor devices that evolved over five generations. Three days later, Hackaday's This Week in Security laid it out cleanly for the hardware crowd: the implant never touches your PC or your WiFi, it never touches the Secure Element. It watches the display. And that is why now.
articles.author: v. Splicer

articles.title: How to Structure a NestJS Backend for AI-Assisted Development
articles.excerpt: AI coding agents are good at writing NestJS code and bad at guessing your NestJS conventions. Left alone, they put queries in controllers, return entities straight from the database, add a fourth way…
articles.body: AI coding agents are good at writing NestJS code and bad at guessing your NestJS conventions. Left alone, they put queries in controllers, return entities straight from the database, add a fourth way of throwing errors, and cheerfully offer to run migration:run against whatever database your .env points at. The fix is not a cleverer prompt. It's a repository that states its rules where agents read them, makes correct changes cheap to verify, and enforces the few rules that must never be broken. Here's the structure I use. None of it needs a particular agent. 1. One instruction file, and only one Every major agent now reads a project instruction file. Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI (with one setting) read AGENTS.md .

articles.title: Giving Your AI Coding Assistant Live Web Access with an MCP Server
articles.excerpt: Large language models know a lot, but they don't know what changed on a website this morning. If you use Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP client, you can close that gap by connecting…
articles.body: Large language models know a lot, but they don't know what changed on a website this morning. If you use Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP client, you can close that gap by connecting a web data server through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This post explains what that gives you, how to set it up in a few minutes, and how to use it without wasting tokens. What MCP adds MCP is an open protocol that lets an AI client call external tools. A web scraping MCP server exposes tools such as "scrape this URL" or "search the web" that the assistant can call on its own when a task needs fresh information: reading the latest docs for a library, checking a changelog, comparing pricing pages, or collecting examples from a site.

But even if you lose, largely speaking, things are going to be fine. Not so in 2021’s Inscryption , a deckbuilder horror game developed by Daniel Mullins Games and published by Devolver Digital, that starts with a haunted card game in a creepy cabin in the woods. But before long, you’ll be eyeing a pair of pliers and wondering which parts of your own body you can live without.

articles.body: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. articles.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, bringing a spectacular display of shooting stars to the autumn sky.
articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
